This post grew out of my diploma thesis in Quantum Information, which
I wrote in Hannover in 2010. The thesis was about quantum memory
channels, and in particular about how deep their memory runs.
Somewhere inside that work a smaller, self-contained question fell
out: how finely can you divide the most destructive process there
is?

The original is written for examiners, not for curious readers. The
arrival of large language models finally removed my last excuse. I
could not resist the temptation to rewrite the thing with agentic
support, trading the terse notation of a thesis for pictures, worked
examples, and a slower pace, so that a motivated undergraduate can
follow every step.

The route, roughly: devices with memory give the problem its
physical face, the classical world gives a first answer, and the
quantum world a quadratically bigger one. Along the way we settle
into a small subclass of channels, simple enough to parameterize by
hand, yet powerful enough to come within a factor of two of the full
quantum answer: the Clifford channels.

Enjoy your read :)
